name: Market participants

subjectOf.text: Trigger designs can be ranked by the certainty they give market participants: institution specific triggers presumably grant the most certainty, while regulatory trigger designs provide lower levels of certainty.
subjectOf.abstract: While institution-specific triggers would presum- ably grant most certainty to market participants, regulatory trig- ger designs could provide lower levels of certainty.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Reflections on the Possible Application of Contingent Capital in Corporate Governance (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=1998455
scope_conditions: comparing institution specific triggers against regulatory or systemic triggers

subjectOf.text: Transfer agents become unnecessary in blockchain based trading models because every function they perform, including maintaining the holding record, can be automated in code and is already produced by the ledger's design.
subjectOf.abstract: In blockchain- based trading models, transfer agents will not be needed because every task they preform can be automated through coding.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
scope_conditions: fully blockchain based trading and settlement models

subjectOf.text: Using blockchain as a more efficient public offering medium will almost certainly require modifying the regulations governing the offering process, the processes for offering, settling, and administering securities, and the roles of market participants built up over decades.
subjectOf.abstract: The utilization of blockchain as a more efficient and reliable public offering medium will almost certainly require modifying many of the (i) regulations applicable to the offering process
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
